faults.evidence: "The Achaeans' harbour was located at the mouth of the Scamander; in Strabo's day the site was some 12 stades from the city" (archive.org-History-20of-20Alexander-3B-20Volume-20I-20Books-20I-III-20-20A.-20B.-20Bosworth-djvu.txt.txt, on 1.11.6)
faults.action: Bosworth (Commentary on 1.11.6) puts the port at the mouth of the Scamander, some 12 stades from Ilium in Strabo's day, and it is drawn there.

faults.evidence: "Arisbe was situated 7~8 km due east of Abydus, in an undulating plain well suited to accommodate a large army" (archive.org-History-20of-20Alexander-3B-20Volume-20I-20Books-20I-III-20-20A.-20B.-20Bosworth-djvu.txt.txt, on 1.12.6)
faults.action: Bosworth (Commentary on 1.12.6) puts Arisbe 7 to 8 km due east of Abydus, in an undulating plain, and it is drawn there.

faults.evidence: "At first he led his forces to the head of the Hellespont, skirting Lampsacus and branching inland south of Parium, so as to avoid the rough passage of the coastline by Priapus." (archive.org-onquest-20and-20Empire-20The-20Reign-20of-20Alexander-20the-20Great-20-281993-29-djvu.txt.txt, ch. 2.III); "Colonae is equally elusive. Strabo locates it 'above Lampsacus and in the mesogaia of Lampsacene' ... This indicates that it was situated inland" and "Hermaeum has been located inland" (archive.org-History-20of-20Alexander-3B-20Volume-20I-20Books-20I-III-20-20A.-20B.-20Bosworth-djvu.txt.txt, on 1.12.6)
faults.action: Colonae and Hermotus have no site in the sources read. Bosworth has the march skirt Lampsacus and turn inland south of Parium, away from the rough coast by Priapus (Conquest and Empire ch. 2.III), with Colonae inland in Lampsacene and Hermotus perhaps Hermaeum, also inland (Commentary on 1.12.6), so the line leaves the coast after Lampsacus. Percote is drawn at Bergaz, about 10 km east of Arisbe on the coast (Commentary on 1.12.6).

faults.evidence: "crossing the river Xanthus, the cities of Pinara, Xanthus, Patara, and about thirty other smaller towns were surrendered to him" (archive.org-download-theanabasisofale46976gut-46976-0.txt.txt, Arrian 1.24); "His route took him through Telmissus to the Xanthos valley, but then he diverged inland through Milyas ... only reaching the coast at Phaselis. He did send forces to occupy the cities of Lower Lycia" (archive.org-onquest-20and-20Empire-20The-20Reign-20of-20Alexander-20the-20Great-20-281993-29-djvu.txt.txt, ch. 2.V). Patara is on the coast, so the route as listed contradicts the Bosworth line its own why follows.
faults.action: [Halicarnassus, Hyparna, Telmissus, Xanthus river, Pinara, Xanthus, Milyas, Phaselis], and the why adds that Patara is among the towns Arrian has surrendered, not a station, and that the start at Halicarnassus is inferred (Arrian 1.24.1 sends the married men home 'from Caria' and names Hyparna as the first place of the route).

faults.evidence: "As he was advancing from Perga, he was met on the road by envoys from the Aspendians ... Alexander then marched to Sidē" (archive.org-download-theanabasisofale46976gut-46976-0.txt.txt, Arrian 1.26). He reaches Aspendus only after Sillyum: "Hearing this, he marched off to Aspendus."
faults.action: [Perge, Side, Sillyum, Aspendus, Perge, Termessus, Sagalassus, Lake Ascania, Celaenae]

faults.evidence: "Thence he went into Phrygia, passing by the lake called Ascania, in which salt is naturally concreted. ... On the fifth day of his march, he arrived at Celaenae" (archive.org-download-theanabasisofale46976gut-46976-0.txt.txt, Arrian 1.29). Arrian does not count the five days from the lake.
faults.action: Arrian names each place, and has him reach Celaenae on the fifth day of the march into Phrygia, past Lake Ascania.

faults.evidence: "Memnon ... acquired possession of Chios ... Thence he sailed to Lesbos" (archive.org-download-theanabasisofale46976gut-46976-0.txt.txt, Arrian 2.1); "conveyed the rest of the army and the stores to Cos" (penelope.uchicago.edu-Thayer-E-Roman-Texts-Diodorus-Siculus-17B.txt, 17.27.5); "Neighbouring Cos had been a base for the Persian fleet since 334" (archive.org-History-20of-20Alexander-3B-20Volume-20I-20Books-20I-III-20-20A.-20B.-20Bosworth-djvu.txt.txt)
faults.action: Arrian and Diodorus give Chios, Lesbos and Mytilene in turn. Neither names Cos as the start: it is the fleet's base after Halicarnassus (Diodorus 17.27.5; Bosworth, Commentary, on Cos as a Persian base since 334), and the line starts there by inference.

faults.evidence: "Fuller at the extreme right, and Bosworth suggests in front of the cavalry as at Gaugamela" (research.md 030.33); plan battles/granicus-334.yaml phases[granicus-vanguard].opens: "archers-agrianians in front of them (Bosworth's suggestion, 030.33, a reconstruction)"; text 020-granicus-vanguard line 7: "they are drawn in front of the Companions"
faults.action: Draw the archers and Agrianians in front of the Companions, as the plan's opens and the page's text say: east of the companions block (u -1150, w -170, depth 200), between it and the river, at about the same u, and end the light-crossing arrow there. As drawn (u -1480, w -220) they stand to the right of and a little behind the Companions, the extreme right that the plan's claim gives as Fuller's place, not Bosworth's. Capture shots/granicus-vanguard.png in the auditor's scratchpad: the block sits south of the Companions under the Alexander marker.

faults.evidence: content/punic-wars/.plans/README.md, Drawing rules: "Place markers beside a block"; battle-auditor definition: "At phone size each unit is apart from its neighbours". Captures in .cache/scratch/030-battle-auditor-granicus-334/.
faults.action: At phone size (390x780) the markers stand on the blocks they name, about 300 m off, less than an icon's width at that scale, so units cannot be told apart or hovered. Phase 1: the Alexander and Amyntas markers cover the companions, archers-agrianians and vanguard blocks; the Memnon marker covers cavalry-left, and SHOT_HOVER at its centre highlights the marker instead of the unit's label (h1p/granicus-vanguard.png). Phase 2: Alexander, Cleitus, Spithridates and Mithridates cover companions, archers-agrianians and vanguard; Parmenion covers the thessalians and the left-crossing arrow; Arsites covers cavalry-centre (shots/granicus-bank.png, crop2.png). Phase 3: the Alexander marker covers phalanx-right's centre (h3m). Move each marker 600 m or more off the blocks onto open ground beside them (the Macedonian markers of phases 1-2 west of the line, the Persian ones east of their blocks), and retake the phone captures.

faults.evidence: "Leading the phalanx against these, and ordering the cavalry to fall upon them from all sides in the midst, he soon cut them up" (archive.org-download-theanabasisofale46976gut-46976-0.txt.txt, Arrian 1.16, in 030.42). No source read names which cavalry rode round which flank.
faults.action: basis: reconstruction, why: "Arrian 1.16.2 has the cavalry fall on them from all sides (030.42) and names no unit; the Companions are drawn on the side where they fought" (and for the thessalians: "...; Parmenion's horse is drawn on the side where it crossed")

faults.evidence: Arrian 1.16.2, "ordering the cavalry to fall upon them from all sides" (archive.org-download-theanabasisofale46976gut-46976-0.txt.txt, in 030.42): the units' flanks are a reconstruction (030-battle-auditor-3), and a reconstruction is told as one.
faults.action: Arrian does not say which horsemen ride where. [The Companions](@granicus-mercenaries-companions) are drawn round their southern flank, and the [Thessalians](@granicus-mercenaries-thessalians) and the allied Greek horse round the northern flank and behind them.

faults.evidence: "finally, the men commanded by Philip, son of Amyntas" (right) and "the brigades of Craterus, Meleager, and Philip, reaching as far as the centre of the entire line" (left) (archive.org-download-theanabasisofale46976gut-46976-0.txt.txt, Arrian 1.14, in 030.30, 030.31); Bosworth on 1.14.2: "There is no justification for supposing ... that the troops involved were anything other than phalanx infantry".
